check: what S1C-DRAIN-01 actually is, and whether newer evidence answers it
theOpenItem: Documents repeatedly record S1C-DRAIN-01 as OPEN, described as STOPPING-time non-zero flights and leases: the run was not fully drained when the server stopped.

whatItWas.state: closed true, failed true, active true
whatItWas.interpretation: Eight flights were still admitted when the snapshot was written, which is the condition the item names.

whatHasChangedSince.codePath: WorldServices line 173 now calls production.close() first and production.export for the STOPPING lifecycle second
whatHasChangedSince.closeBehaviour: ProductionWallPipeline.close completes every flight exceptionally and clears the map, then closes and clears leases, so both collections are empty by construction before the snapshot is written
whatHasChangedSince.commentInCode: Reservation owners release only after their entered producer and consumer chains quiesce; closing admissions cannot make still-live T0 or compiled objects unaccounted.

newerEvidence.failure: creation token required for history - a different defect, since fixed
newerEvidence.interpretation: Every drain counter is zero at STOPPING under the current ordering, which is the condition the item asks for.

conclusion: The specific symptom the item names no longer reproduces: the newest available STOPPING snapshot shows all counters at zero. The documents still calling it OPEN predate the close-then-export ordering.
whatThisDoesNotProve: One clean snapshot is not the same as the item being formally closed, and the 24h profile will produce a STOPPING snapshot of its own. Recorded as evidence bearing on the item, not as a signature closing it.
head: 6856e92
correctedOn20261007: The conclusion above is too strong and is withdrawn. The all-zero snapshot it relies on comes from a run that FAILED - state failed true and closed true, failure 'creation token required for history'. A failed run tears down, and teardown zeroes the counters by construction, so that snapshot cannot show whether the drain completes on a successful run. The project had already reached this conclusion in S1C-OwnerCoverage-A+C状态.md line 53, which declines the same snapshot as insufficient to close the item. What stands from this file is the definition of the item and the close-then-export ordering; what does not stand is the claim that the item is answered. Settling it needs a STOPPING snapshot from a run that succeeded.
